text: A subgroup N ≤ G satisfying gng⁻¹ ∈ N for all g ∈ G and n ∈ N is called a ___ subgroup; these are exactly the subgroups by which one can form a quotient group.
explanation: Normality (gng⁻¹ ∈ N) is precisely the condition that makes the quotient group G/N well defined under (gN)(hN) = (gh)N, and kernels of homomorphisms are always normal.
